model_result.answer_summary: P6 has 6 x 14 = 84 pi electrons in its global circuit. The least positive removal producing a Huckel 4k+2 count is 2, leaving 82 = 4 x 20 + 2 pi electrons. Therefore n(e) = 2 and n(t) = 82.
assumptions: Source-image encoding: P6 contains six porphyrin--butadiyne repeat units.
Source-image electron count: one continuous global route contributes five pi-electron pairs through the porphyrin and two through the butadiyne linker, i.e. 14 pi electrons per repeat.
Huckel aromaticity is represented exactly as a natural-number electron count of the form 4k+2.
An oxidative removal is a positive natural number no greater than the neutral global-circuit electron count.
